questions.title: Sum of First N Natural Numbers
questions.description:
Read an integer n and print the sum of all natural numbers from 1 to n using a for loop.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
One line containing the sum 1 + 2 + ... + n.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000

questions.title: Multiplication Table
questions.description:
Read an integer n and print its multiplication table from 1 to 10, one line per row.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
10 lines, each in the form: n x i = product (for i from 1 to 10).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20

questions.title: Canteen Daily Sales Report
questions.description:
The college canteen recorded the order amount of every customer today. Given n customers and their order amounts, walk the amounts with a single for loop and produce the day's report: the total sales and the highest single order.

Input Format:
The first token is n. The next n tokens are the order amounts.

Output Format:
Line 1: Total: <sum of all amounts>
Line 2: Highest: <largest single amount>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= amount <= 10000

questions.title: First N Fibonacci Numbers
questions.description:
The math club wants a poster showing the first n Fibonacci numbers, starting from 0 and 1 (0 1 1 2 3 5 ...). Print them on one line separated by single spaces. Values grow quickly, so use long arithmetic.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
One line with the first n Fibonacci numbers separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50

questions.title: Factorial Using while
questions.description:
Read an integer n and print n factorial (1 x 2 x ... x n) using a while loop. Note that 20! exceeds the range of int, so accumulate in a long.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
One line containing n!.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20

questions.title: Count the Digits
questions.description:
Read an integer n and count how many digits it has using a while loop that divides the number by 10 repeatedly until it becomes 0.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of digits.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000000000

questions.title: Savings Goal with Monthly Interest
questions.description:
Aarav opens a savings account with an initial balance and deposits a fixed amount at the start of every month. At the end of each month the bank adds 2 percent interest, computed with integer math as balance = balance + balance * 2 / 100. Simulate month by month with a while loop until the balance reaches or exceeds the target, then report the number of months needed and the final balance (if the initial balance already meets the target, 0 months pass).

Input Format:
One line with three integers: initial balance, monthly deposit, and target.

Output Format:
Line 1: the number of months needed.
Line 2: the final balance.

Constraints:
1 <= initial <= 10000, 1 <= deposit <= 1000, 1 <= target <= 1000000

questions.title: Collatz Longest Chain
questions.description:
A math hobbyist studies the Collatz rule: for an even value the next value is value / 2, and for an odd value it is 3 * value + 1; every starting value eventually reaches 1. For every starting value from a to b (inclusive), count the number of steps needed to reach 1. Report the starting value with the longest chain and its step count. If several values tie, the smallest of them wins: scan from a upward and keep only strictly greater improvements.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b.

Output Format:
Line 1: the starting value with the most steps.
Line 2: that step count.

Constraints:
1 <= a <= b <= 10000

questions.title: Sum Until the Zero Sentinel
questions.description:
A cashier terminal accepts integers one by one until the sentinel value 0 appears; the 0 ends the session and is not counted as a sale. Read the values with a do-while loop and print the sum of all values before the sentinel.

Input Format:
A sequence of integers terminated by 0 (the final 0 ends the input).

Output Format:
One line with the sum of all values before the sentinel.

Constraints:
1 to 1000 values before the sentinel 0, each between -10000 and 10000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 to 1000 values before the sentinel 0, each between -10000 and 10000

questions.title: Launch Countdown Timer
questions.description:
Mission control runs a launch countdown: starting from n, print one number per line down to 1, then print Liftoff!. Use a do-while loop so the countdown body always executes at least once.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
One line per countdown value from n down to 1, followed by the line Liftoff!.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100

questions.title: ATM PIN Retry
questions.description:
An ATM asks for a PIN and keeps prompting until the correct one is entered. The first token of the input is the correct PIN, followed by the PINs the customer actually typed, in order; the last attempt always matches. Simulate the retries with a do-while loop (each attempt must be checked after it is read) and print which attempt number finally grants access.

Input Format:
The first token is the correct PIN. The remaining tokens are the entered PINs in order; the last of them equals the correct PIN.

Output Format:
One line: Access granted on attempt X, where X is the 1-based number of the matching attempt.

Constraints:
PIN strings of 1 to 8 digits, at most 5 attempts, the last attempt is correct
questions.inputconstrains: PIN strings of 1 to 8 digits, at most 5 attempts, the last attempt is correct

questions.title: Digit Frequency Report
questions.description:
An auditor examines an account number and counts how many times each digit 0-9 occurs inside it. Extract the digits with a do-while loop (so the number 0 is also handled correctly), then print one line for every digit that occurs at least once, in ascending digit order.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
For each digit d that occurs in n, in ascending digit order: Digit d: count

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000000000
questions.output2:
Digit 0: 1
Digit 1: 1
Digit 2: 1
Digit 3: 1
Digit 4: 1
Digit 5: 1
Digit 6: 1
Digit 7: 1
Digit 8: 1
Digit 9: 1

questions.title: Array Sum with Enhanced For
questions.description:
Read n integers into an int array, then use an enhanced for loop (for(int v : array)) to compute and print their sum.

Input Format:
The first token is n. The next n tokens are the array elements.

Output Format:
One line with the sum of all elements.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, each element between -1000000 and 1000000

questions.title: Shop Billing Total
questions.description:
A shopkeeper bills n customers, one item each. Read the n prices into an array, then walk the array with an enhanced for loop and report the day's total sales and how many premium items (price strictly greater than 100) were sold.

Input Format:
The first token is n. The next n tokens are the prices.

Output Format:
Line 1: Total: <sum of all prices>
Line 2: Premium items: <count of prices greater than 100>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= price <= 10000

questions.title: Temperature Min and Max in One Pass
questions.description:
A weather station logged n temperature readings for the day. Using a single enhanced for loop pass (no sorting, no Math.max or Math.min), find the lowest and the highest reading.

Input Format:
The first token is n. The next n tokens are the readings.

Output Format:
Line 1: Min: <lowest reading>
Line 2: Max: <highest reading>

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, each reading between -50 and 60

questions.title: Runner-Up Score Hunt
questions.description:
A gaming leaderboard stores n scores. Without sorting the array, use enhanced for loops to find the champion score and then the best score that is strictly below it (the runner-up). If every score is identical, the runner-up does not exist.

Input Format:
The first token is n. The next n tokens are the scores.

Output Format:
One line with the runner-up score, or the single line No second place when all scores are equal.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= score <= 1000000000

questions.title: Cinema Seat Map
questions.description:
A cinema's ticketing screen shows the seat map for a hall with n rows and m seats in each row, every seat drawn as a star. Print the map with nested loops: one line per row and m stars on each line.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: rows and seats per row.

Output Format:
n lines, each containing m star characters.

Constraints:
1 <= rows <= 20, 1 <= seats <= 20

questions.title: Right-Angled Star Triangle
questions.description:
For the school's annual day banner, print a right-angled star triangle with n rows: row i (1-based) contains exactly i star characters. Build it with nested for loops, printing the stars of each row and then moving to the next line.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
n lines; line i contains i star characters.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50

questions.title: Perfect Numbers in a Range
questions.description:
The math society hunts perfect numbers: a number is perfect when it equals the sum of its proper divisors (for example 6 = 1 + 2 + 3). Scan every number from a to b; for each one add up its divisors from 1 up to n / 2 with an inner loop, then compare the sum with the number itself. Print every perfect number found, one per line in ascending order; if the range contains none, print None.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b.

Output Format:
One line per perfect number in ascending order, or the single line None if there is no perfect number in the range.

Constraints:
1 <= a <= b <= 10000

questions.title: Digit Pyramid
questions.description:
Print a centered digit pyramid with n rows. Row i starts with (n - i) leading spaces, then the digits 1 to i in ascending order, then the digits i - 1 down to 1. The leading spaces are part of the output and must be printed exactly.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
n lines forming the pyramid.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 9
